From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>

Subject: Order form — initial redlines and invoice entity question

Hi team,

Thanks for sending over the draft order form. I reviewed the commercial sections with Ben and Karthik this morning and attached a redline (Acme_Order_Form_v3_redline.pdf) that captures a few items we need clarified before we can proceed to signature:

- Invoice recipient / legal entity: our Finance team needs confirmation which Acme legal entity will accept the invoices (billing entity + VAT handling). We flagged the Order Form to allow invoicing to either Acme Hospitality Inc. or Acme Europe Ltd; please confirm preferred entity and any tax residency docs required.
- Net payment terms: Acme requested Net-60 in the markup. Our standard on this deal cadence had been Net-45; Ben has included a recommended schedule in pricing_schedule_v4.xlsx. Can you confirm whether Net-60 is firm or negotiable?
- Minimum commit phasing: we proposed a two-tranche minimum commit in section 2.2 to match your implementation timeline; confirm whether the first tranche needs to be invoiced up front or can be milestone-based.
- Taxes and withholding: if Acme is required to withhold VAT or other taxes, please confirm whether you will provide the appropriate certificate/evidence to prevent gross-up.

Attachments: Acme_Order_Form_v3_redline.pdf (pdf, 224KB), pricing_schedule_v4.xlsx (xlsx, 34KB).

Next steps: once we have confirmation on entity and net terms we can finalize the order form and route to Legal for a quick signoff (we expect 1–2 business days for minor redlines). If you prefer, we can join a 30-minute alignment call — Ben and Karthik are available Thursday afternoon.

Thanks,

Kimberly Park

Subject: Re: Order form — initial redlines and invoice entity question

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks for the redline; I reviewed with Acme Finance and Legal. A few clarifications from our side:

1) Invoice entity: Acme Hospitality Inc. (US entity) will receive all invoices for the first 12 months. After that, we may transition EMEA bookings to Acme Europe Ltd. Please add "Invoices to: Acme Hospitality Inc., EIN: 12-3456789, Attn: AP" to the order form. We will provide any tax residency docs on request.

2) Net terms: Procurement would prefer Net-60 due to internal approvals. Finance is okay with Net-60 for the first year if Redwood agrees to a 1.0% early-pay discount for Net-30 settlement on invoice lines paid within 30 days. Is that acceptable?

3) Minimum commit: We accept the two-tranche plan but request the first tranche be invoiced at contract signature (tranche A) and the second tranche invoiced at the start of Q3. If Redwood requires milestone-based invoicing instead, please propose precise milestone definitions.

4) Taxes/withholding: Acme will not withhold U.S. federal taxes but may have VAT or local indirect tax obligations in EMEA rollouts. We will provide certificates for any withholding exemptions.

If those points are acceptable, I can return a clean copy for signature. Otherwise, happy to hop on a short call with Ben and Karthik to speed this up.

Best,

Emily Cho
Senior Counsel — Commercial Contracts
Acme Hospitality
emily.cho@acme.com
